candidates.title: Crown says DNA evidence helped ID man now on trial for decades-old sex assaults against children
candidates.description: Prosecutors told a jury in Brampton, Ont., on Monday, how DNA evidence had linked three brutal attacks against children in the 1990s to Richard Neil, now 67 and on trial for charges including kidnapping, sexual assault causing bodily harm and administering a stupefying drug.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: ‘Toothpaste is out of the tube': Pro-separation advertiser says further action needed against Forever Canadian
candidates.description: A third-party advertiser campaigning in favour of Alberta separation said it is “better late than never” after Elections Alberta told a pro-Confederation group to disclose some campaign expenses.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tesla's exclusion from Manitoba EV program 'incredibly unfair,' politically motivated, court hears
candidates.description: Who in the Manitoba government decided to exclude Tesla from the province's electric vehicle rebate program, and why, is still unclear following a court hearing on the decision, the company's lawyers argue.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 2 Canadian Armed Forces members arrested in organized crime, kidnapping probe, DND says
candidates.description: The Department of National Defence says two members of the Canadian Armed Forces were arrested by Toronto police on charges related to organized crime, kidnapping and firearms theft.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alleged NATO spy case brings 'some serious lessons' for Canada, public safety minister says
candidates.description: Public Safety Minister Gary Anandasangaree says "gaps" in Canada's security screening need to be addressed following the arrest of a Canadian NATO intern in Belgium on espionage charges.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Man accused in massive gold heist at Toronto's Pearson airport pleads not guilty as trial begins
candidates.description: A man accused in what investigators have called one of the largest gold heists in Canadian history has pleaded not guilty to two charges as his trial begins in Brampton, Ont.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Supreme Court's top judge starts judicial year by stressing need to protect democratic institutions
candidates.description: Canada's democratic institutions need protection in the face of unrelenting pressures, Chief Justice Richard Wagner said on Monday as the Supreme Court of Canada opened a new judicial year.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: ‘Unintended consequences’: Poll shows UCP independence referendum boosting Alberta NDP
candidates.description: Premier Danielle Smith's efforts to satisfy the party faithful with an independence referendum may have unintentionally breathed life into the opposition NDP.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: SCO condemns Winnipeg Sun, mayoral-candidate CEO for column questioning deaths at residential schools
candidates.description: A column questioning the deaths of children at residential schools has led the Southern Chiefs’ Organization to condemn the Winnipeg Sun and express concern that the newspaper’s CEO is running for mayor of the Manitoba capital.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Canadians born abroad caught up in yearslong citizenship certificate processing delays
candidates.description: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada is struggling to handle a flood of citizenship applications — many of them from a change to federal law late last year that allows anyone who can prove they have a Canadian ancestor to apply. That backlog is preventing some Canadians born abroad from coming home.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta lawyers urge province to publicly release long-awaited review of police misconduct probes
candidates.description: More than 22 months since an independent review got underway to examine how the Alberta Crown Prosecution Service handles police misconduct investigations, members of the legal community are calling on the province to make the final report public.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: $100K Giller Prize announces 5-title shortlist for 2026
candidates.description: The Giller Prize annually recognizes the best in Canadian fiction. The five authors shortlisted are Tara Gereaux, Michelle Good, Nicholas Herring, Nazanine Hozar and Patmeena Sabit.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Heartbreaking reality': Crew, passengers of downed medical transport jet are likely dead, company says
candidates.description: The decision by the U.S. Coast Guard to end the search for the crew and passengers of a medical transport jet out of Hamilton, Ont., means it's time to accept that the four Canadians and two Bermudians on board didn't survive, says the company that operated the jet.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Alberta's population grew by more people than any other place in Canada, data shows
candidates.description: Alberta’s population continues to grow — and faster than almost all of Canada, Statistics Canada’s latest population estimates suggest.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Build Canada Homes was launched a year ago. Can it scale up fast enough to meet demand?
candidates.description: Build Canada Homes promises to scale up the delivery of affordable housing at a time when industry leaders are raising the alarm about the lagging pace of housing development across the country. After one year of existence, the agency has only begun construction of about 2,000 units.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: After years of calls for data, study confirms Black Canadians face higher risk of maternal complications
candidates.description: The most comprehensive study yet of maternal health in Canada has found that Black Canadians face a much higher risk of serious complications during pregnancy, labour, delivery and postpartum than white people — underlining the urgent need for better data tracking and tools to eliminate systemic anti-Black racism in our health-care system, researchers and advocates say.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cold reality: Canadian troops struggle in Alaska as military relearns Arctic warfare
candidates.description: Canadian troops battled frostbite, failing batteries, communications problems and gaps in basic winter skills during a major Alaska exercise, according to an internal evaluation. Despite achieving their training objectives, the experience exposed how much the military must relearn as Ottawa promises a larger, sustained presence — and credible combat capability — in the Arctic.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Student reportedly loses hand from police grenade amid France's education protests
candidates.description: A teenager's hand was blown off as high-school protesters clashed with riot police in northern France on Monday, a local official said, on ‌the eve of a national demonstration by the pupils' union against underfunding, overcrowding and dilapidation.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New York state declares measles disaster emergency
candidates.description: New York Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency on Monday over a measles outbreak, the first such declaration ​by a U.S. state since cases began surging in ​2025. New York has reported 108 measles ‌cases so far this year, with seven cases in New York City and 101 elsewhere in the state.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor challenges validity of search warrants in his Epstein-related arrest
candidates.description: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is taking the police to court to challenge his February arrest on suspicion of misconduct in public office over allegations he sent confidential government documents to Jeffrey Epstein.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Tennis player Daniil Medvedev disqualified from China Open semifinal for hitting fan with ball during match
candidates.description: Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from his semifinal against Novak Djokovic at the China Open after he hit a ball into the stands that struck a spectator in the front row on Monday in Beijing.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Avengers: Endgame once again beats Avatar as highest-grossing movie of all time
candidates.description: Marvel's Avengers: Endgame has recaptured its title as the highest-grossing movie of all time this weekend (not accounting for inflation). It overtook James Cameron's biggest release with a gross of $2.9255 billion US, narrowly superseding Avatar's $2.9237 billion US.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Norway seeks temporary ban on smart glasses amid privacy concerns
candidates.description: Norwegian authorities say a ban on the use of smart glasses could apply to places where "privacy is particularly important," like health-care facilities or fitness centres with changing rooms and showers.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Israeli officials say FlyDubai co-pilot planned attack before joining airline
candidates.description: U.A.E. authorities and FlyDubai have not publicly disclosed the identity of the co-pilot, who stabbed his captain in ‌a suspected attempt to crash a plane en route to Ben Gurion International Airport near Tel Aviv last week.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Nobel Prize in Medicine awarded to scientists who pioneered work in optogenetics
candidates.description: Scientists Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg ‌Nagel won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or ​Medicine for "discoveries concerning light-gated ​ion channels and optogenetics," the award-giving body ​said Monday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Spanish PM calls snap election amid mounting housing crisis
candidates.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called an early election for Nov. 29 on Monday, in a bid to strengthen his mandate after a fragmented parliament rejected the government's key housing decrees last week amid widespread protests.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: After Trump’s Venezuelan oil deal, those living on polluted lake in oil country wait for change
candidates.description: In late August, the U.S. signed a sweeping oil deal with Venezuela's interim authorities to control a share of the country's oil. In one of the largest oil-producing regions, residents welcome promises to revitalize the industry, they also have a more immediate demand: clean up the polluted lake.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Jane Doe at centre of Cornell rape case targeted with threats, her lawyer says
candidates.description: The woman who has alleged she was drugged and raped by ‌Cornell University students has been the target of threats, her lawyer said on Sunday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump names U.S. intelligence chief Jay Clayton as new AI czar
candidates.description: Clayton, director of U.S. national intelligence, will head the Trump administration's newly created AI task force, the "Super Intelligence Force."
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: U.S. removes B-1 bombers from U.K. airbase targeted in suspected plot: Pentagon
candidates.description: A dozen B-1 bombers used in U.S. strikes on Iran had been deployed to RAF Fairford, northwest of London, which was targeted in a suspected terror plot.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Serb nationalist credits Trump, Putin after declaring his party's victory in Bosnian election
candidates.description: Bosnian Serb nationalist politician Milorad Dodik has declared victory for his party in an election in Bosnia on Sunday that was shaped by economic pressures, the prospect of the Balkan nation joining the European Union and ethnic tensions that have divided the country since its brutal 1992-95 war.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Lula and Bolsonaro head to run-off in Brazil's presidential election
candidates.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, an ally of U.S. President Donald Trump, and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil's veteran president, will face off on Oct. 25 in a run-off for the top job of Latin America's powerhouse economy.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Everyone knew': Canadian men's coach Jesse Marsch calls for severe punishment for Manchester City over financial breaches
candidates.description: Canadian men's soccer coach ​Jesse Marsch has called for Manchester City to be punished severely over breaches of Premier League financial rules, saying his experience managing against the club left him convinced there were inconsistencies in the way it operated.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cornell president calls alleged gang rape 'deeply disturbing,' pledges greater transparency
candidates.description: Scrutiny has mounted in recent days over Cornell's response to allegations that the woman was sexually assaulted by multiple fraternity members in 2024. The woman, identified in court documents as Jane Doe, has sued the university and seven former students.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: The King will never live at Buckingham Palace. What does that mean for the monarchy?
candidates.description: While there have been efforts to emphasize that Buckingham Palace will continue to be the working and ceremonial headquarters of the monarchy, the recent confirmation that King Charles won’t be living there could also be sending signals about the institution and its future.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Cenovus Energy signs deal to buy Athabasca Oil in deal valued at $5.7 billion
candidates.description: Cenovus CEO Jon McKenzie says Athabasca's high-quality, long-life assets fit the company's portfolio and provide a clear opportunity to improve performance, grow production and create long-term shareholder value.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Suncor selling off stakes in N.L.’s Terra Nova, White Rose and West White Rose for $1.2B
candidates.description: Calgary-based Suncor Energy is selling off stakes in three Newfoundland and Labrador oilfields — Terra Nova, White Rose and West White Rose — to Ithaca Energy in a deal for $1.2 billion plus up to $350 million based on future oil prices. The deal is expected to close in early 2027.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says 'threat' led US to pull bombers from RAF Fairford
candidates.description: The Pentagon confirmed on Sunday it had removed the B1 bombers from the base in England back to their home stations in America.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: France braces for national day of school protests after injuries and mass arrests
candidates.description: France prepares for a day of protests in support of students who’ve been demanding more investment in education.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Zelensky condemns 'horrific' Russian strike on boat carrying corn in Black Sea
candidates.description: The vessel's captain was killed and 11 crew members were rescued after the attack on the Turkish-owned ship, Ukraine's leader says.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Spain PM pins hopes on housing crisis to help win snap election
candidates.description: Calling of a snap election was not a knee-jerk reaction from Pedro Sánchez but a carefully thought-out manoeuvre, Guy Hedgecoe reports from Madrid.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US 'watching closely' after plague researcher dies in Russia
candidates.description: Donald Trump says the US was looking "very strongly" at the case of a lab technician who died at a research centre in Siberia.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Pentagon stops using Anthropic AI tools after blacklisting company, BBC told
candidates.description: It labelled Anthropic a "supply chain risk" in February after the firm refused to remove safety guardrails from its tools.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Nobel Prize awarded for revealing inner workings of the brain
candidates.description: US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have been awarded for their work.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Right-wing Flávio Bolsonaro wins first round of Brazil election
candidates.description: With neither candidate getting more than 50% of the vote, the election will go to a run-off on 25 October.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Georgia officials hunt for suspect in shooting that killed two and injured 35
candidates.description: A homecoming celebration turned into a scene of deadly violence, as dozens of shots were fired into a crowd.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Bombs preventing rescue of kidnapped youths, Nigerian police say
candidates.description: The father of one of the 19 young abductees tells the BBC he hasn't eaten in three days out of worry.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Yemeni military says it has retaken Mokha and 'secured' Red Sea waterway
candidates.description: Saudi-backed forces say they seized the port city of Mocha, near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, at the start of an offensive against the Houthis.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: £800m in, £800m out - Why Man City scandal shines light on Man Utd finances
candidates.description: Manchester City's owners have been found guilty of injecting money into the club. At Manchester United, fans are frustrated at how much has been taken out.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Indian singer Anuv Jain on finding success without the Bollywood boost
candidates.description: The star reveals why he is "very selective" about releasing music - and shares his future collab hopes.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why Canada is wargaming a (long shot) US invasion
candidates.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the military is running scenarios in the unlikely case the US invades Canada.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Watch: How Brazil's dramatic election unfolded
candidates.description: Millions of Brazilians took to the polls on Sunday for the first round of the country's presidential elections.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Drones buzz overhead, troops hunker underground in Ukraine's hellish kill zone
candidates.description: The front line in the Russia-Ukraine war stretches more than 700 miles and has barely moved in four years. Yet straddling this line is the kill zone, dominated by constantly evolving drone technology.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: FBI arrests a woman accused of spying on Taiwan leader's family for China
candidates.description: The FBI and U.S. prosecutors say Wanying Zhang, also know as Heather, surveilled the Taiwanese president's son and his family.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Imran Khan supporters march in Pakistan to demand his release after talks failed
candidates.description: Talks between Khan's party and the government failed two days ago. Besides Khan's release, protesters demand his transfer to a hospital and family visits.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: SCOTUS hears major climate change case. And, Brazil's presidential race goes to runoff
candidates.description: The Supreme Court is set to hear a blockbuster climate change case that could affect more than just climate issues. And, Brazil's presidential race is too close to call.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: FlyDubai attacker intended to crash plane into Tel Aviv airport, investigation finds
candidates.description: The ongoing investigation has found the attacker intended to crash the plane into Israel's Ben Gurion International Airport, a person familiar with the matter but not authorized to speak publicly told NPR.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. Marine suspected in woman's death arrested in Japan
candidates.description: A U.S. Marine has been arrested on suspicion of murder in Okinawa, prompting renewed Japanese criticism of the conduct of American military personnel.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Nobel medicine prize goes to 3 scientists for research into brain activity
candidates.description: The Nobel Prize in medicine was awarded Monday to three scientists working on the mechanisms the brain uses to switch on, or off, the activity of individual nerve cells.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Former Prince Andrew files legal action to quash warrants that led to residence searches
candidates.description: A judicial spokesperson confirmed that Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor had filed a claim with the High Court in London and a hearing would take place Thursday.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Spain's prime minister calls early elections as pressure mounts over housing crisis
candidates.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced early elections Monday after his government suffered a bruising legislative defeat last week on emergency measures related to the country's housing crisis.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: G7 countries reluctantly agree to tap their fuel reserves to help the U.S.
candidates.description: G7 nations plan to release large amounts of diesel fuel soon, but European countries were not entirely happy about the agreement.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: She died covering war for Fox News. Her parents blame the network — and a star reporter
candidates.description: The family members of two Fox News journalists killed while covering the war in Ukraine are suing the network, saying it put getting the story ahead of its people.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Republicans and Democrats find a unifying target: Pharmacy benefit managers
candidates.description: Republicans and Democrats, both patients and politicians, seem united in their disdain for the healthcare companies known as pharmacy benefit managers. Tennessee and Arkansas are regulating them now.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: From floating saunas to clinical trials: How heat might help mental health
candidates.description: While scientists have a decent understanding of how sauna and other forms of heat exposure exercises our cardiovascular system, they know relatively little about its impact on mental health.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: What does marathon training do to your body? A reporter becomes the test subject
candidates.description: Before running the New York City Marathon, NPR's Elissa Nadworny gets a bone scan, blood work and a treadmill test to settle a question from Mom: Is this bad for my body?
candidates.author: NPR
